08:45 Local Time, 03:15 GMT, 08:45 IST: It's the start of an important Test series in Sri Lanka and we are at the picturesque Galle International Stadium, a venue each cricket purist should try to visit for a Test match. The Fort in the background, the coastline... the drone shots from the host broadcaster these days are a sight to behold. This is generally a result-oriented venue. There has been only one draw (rain-marred) here in the last 27 Tests since 2014. Spin usually plays a massive role but will that be the case again?

Weather check: There has been rain in the build up to this game. The ground was covered on the eve of the game and some overnight rain is also expected. The radar is largely showing post-play rains for the first, two days and as of now, the third day forecast isn't pretty, with weather expected to halt play. But, this is Sri Lanka and things can quickly change. Because of the rain, the pitch is feared to be not as dry as Galle usually is. Does this mean it will turn slightly less? That's what the Sri Lankan captain Dhananjaya de Silva felt pre-match, hinting at a better batting surface. "It's hard to predict exactly how it will play because with the weather around, they haven't been able to dry it as they normally might," DDS said.
On their 80th Independence Day, Shubman Gill will have the honour of leading India in their historic 600th Test match. Only England and Australia have played more Tests.
